raw_case_text:
A 35-year-old femalepresented with widespread painful crusted skin lesions over both palms and digits [Figure 1]. The largest lesion ranged from 3 cm x 5 cm and the smallest from 2 cm x 2 cm. They were preceded by discrete deep-seated vesicles 2 weeks earlier, which ruptured within a day or two and coalesced to form plaques with minimal discharge. On examination, well-demarcated plaques were present, associated with thick, adherent reddish yellow crusts, accompanied by a foul-smelling odor and tenderness. Contracture of the middle finger of the right hand was observed owing to similar lesions in the past.
Further, genital examination revealed numerous painful genital ulcers over the labia majora, labia minora, and inner aspect of the thigh covered with a pale creamy discharge [Figure 2]. The inguinal lymph nodes were enlarged and tender. The lesions over the hand and genitalia appeared simultaneously.
The history of a similar episode was present 2 years ago; however, the treatment details could not be traced. She was diagnosed to be HIV positive 10 years ago and has been on regular "highly active antiretroviral treatment" since then. Her CD4 count at the time of presentation to us was 236 cells/mm.
Bacterial and fungal cultures failed to show any growth. Biopsy displayed nonspecific features and the laboratory parameters were unremarkable except for hemoglobin of 9.2 g%. The serological test for HSV IgM was strongly positive. Polymerase chain reaction and viral cultures could not be carried out due to unavailability and cost constraints.
Episodic treatment with tablet acyclovir 400 mg per oral, 5 times daily, was started for 2 weeks until the lesions healed completely.
One month later, she presented again with vesicles over the palms and with genital ulcers, and contractures from the previous episode were evident [Figure 1]. Biopsy of the vesicle for histopathological examination was consistent with herpes virus infection revealing an intraepidermal vesicle containing balloon cells, neutrophils, nuclear debris, and fibrin strands. Balloon cells were noted to have pale gray nuclei, some being multinucleated. Dense mononuclear infiltrate was present in the upper dermis [Figure 3].
The patient was commenced on suppressive therapy with tablet acyclovir 400 mg orally, 2 times daily, to which she responded satisfactorily. Follow-up at 6 months showed no new lesions.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old female presenting with painful, foul-smelling, crusted skin plaques over both hands and painful genital ulcers for two weeks.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 2-week history of painful lesions simultaneously erupting on both hands and the genital region. The hand lesions began as discrete, deep-seated vesicles that ruptured within 1 to 2 days and coalesced into tender, foul-smelling, crusted plaques. She reported a similar episode 2 years prior that had resulted in a flexion contracture of her right middle finger. Following treatment and complete healing, she presented one month later with recurrent palmar vesicles and genital ulcerations.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underlying chronic retroviral illness diagnosed 10 years earlier, maintained on regular highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART); history of a similar blistering and ulcerating episode 2 years prior resulting in digital contracture.
subjective.review_of_systems: Painful cutaneous and genital lesions, foul-smelling discharge, and local tenderness; denies systemic fever, chills, or gastrointestinal complaints.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic/Extremities: Well-demarcated plaques measuring from 2 cm x 2 cm up to 3 cm x 5 cm over both palms and digits, covered with thick, adherent reddish-yellow crusts, foul-smelling discharge, and local tenderness; flexion contracture of the right middle finger. Genitourinary: Numerous exquisitely painful ulcers over the labia majora, labia minora, and inner thighs covered with pale creamy exudate. Lymphatics: Tender bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 9.2 g%; remaining routine laboratory hematologic and biochemical parameters were unremarkable. Bacterial and fungal cultures: No microbial growth.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin biopsy of initial lesion: Non-specific inflammatory changes. Skin biopsy of recurrent palm vesicle: Intraepidermal blister containing balloon cells with pale gray nuclei and multinucleation, neutrophils, nuclear debris, and fibrin strands, accompanied by dense upper dermal mononuclear infiltrate, consistent with viral cytopathic changes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe, atypical, recalcitrant herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection causing synchronous crusted palmar plaques (herpetic geometric ecchymosis/whitlow) and genital herpes in a patient with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (CD4 cell count 236 cells/mm3). Diagnostic confirmation: Strongly positive serum HSV IgM serology, supported by classic cytopathic histopathologic features of multinucleated balloon cells on repeat lesional biopsy; bacterial and fungal cultures were negative. Management & Outcome: Acute episode treated with oral acyclovir 400 mg 5 times daily for 2 weeks, resulting in complete lesion re-epithelialization. Upon clinical recurrence 1 month later, initiated on chronic oral acyclovir suppressive therapy at 400 mg twice daily, achieving satisfactory remission without new lesions at 6 months of follow-up.
